evidence.intro: AI output is separated into two kinds of statements, so the source of each claim stays visible.

finding.title: Finding
finding.description: A statement grounded in a source passage, shown with its quote and citation.

interpretation.title: AI interpretation
interpretation.description: A conclusion drawn across findings, clearly labelled and linked to supporting evidence.

evidence.question: Can I trace a finding back to its source?
evidence.answer: Yes. Findings are linked to their supporting passage and citation; AI interpretations are labelled separately and link to findings.

sources.question: Do I need to start with PDFs?
sources.answer: No. You can also add page images, web links, pasted text, or papers found through search.

privacy.question: Who can see my sources?
privacy.answer: Sources are private to the project owner and invited project members unless you choose to publish a synthesis.

languages.question: Which languages does Skimr support?
languages.answer: The interface is designed for English, French, and Spanish. Source quotations remain in their original language.

cta.heading: Make your next literature review easier to verify
cta.description: Bring your sources into one workspace and keep the evidence close to every finding.

web_and_pasted_sources.title: Web links and pasted text

about.title: About Skimr | Research, grounded in evidence
about.description: Skimr is a research workspace for organizing academic sources and building evidence-backed literature reviews.
about.heading: About Skimr
about.intro: Skimr helps students, researchers, research assistants, and policy analysts organize sources and understand how findings relate.
about.evidence_description: A finding should lead back to the passage it came from. An AI interpretation should be labelled and supported by findings, not presented as a source fact.

privacy.title: Privacy policy | Skimr
privacy.description: Learn how Skimr handles private research sources, image metadata, and the Gemini free-tier OCR fallback.
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: Skimr is designed to help you work with research sources in private projects. This page summarizes the source-handling practices in the product specification.
privacy.private_sources_heading: Your sources stay within your project
privacy.private_sources_description: Uploaded files, OCR text, and web snapshots are stored privately for research. They are available only to the project owner and invited project members unless you choose to publish a synthesis.
privacy.images_description: Uploaded page images are re-encoded to remove metadata, including location information, before they are stored.
privacy.gemini_description: When OCR confidence is low, a limited number of pages may be sent to Google's Gemini free tier as an OCR fallback. Google may use free-tier requests to improve its products. Do not upload confidential or unpublished work for this fallback.

terms.title: Terms of use | Skimr
terms.description: Read the basic rules for uploading research material and keeping sources private in Skimr.
terms.heading: Terms of use
terms.intro: Use Skimr only with material you are entitled to use and upload.
terms.rights_heading: Your right to use uploaded material
terms.rights_description: You are responsible for ensuring that you have the right to access and upload each source, and for following any applicable copyright, licence, and institutional requirements.
terms.private_sources_description: Sources are stored privately for research and are visible only to the project owner and invited members. Do not upload material you are not permitted to share with the service.
terms.public_synthesis_description: A public synthesis is read-only and may be indexed. It can contain short source quotations of at most two sentences each, with links to the originals; it does not display full source text, images, or snapshots.

cookies.title: Cookies | Skimr
cookies.description: Learn about Skimr's theme preference storage and the authentication cookie used in the dashboard.
cookies.heading: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.intro: Skimr uses browser storage for preferences and an essential authentication cookie for signed-in sessions.
cookies.theme_description: The public site stores your light, dark, or system theme preference in localStorage. This preference is not a cookie.
cookies.authentication_description: When you sign in, the dashboard uses a secure, HTTP-only, SameSite=Strict refresh cookie so JavaScript cannot read the token. It is limited to authentication routes and is used to maintain your session.
